angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 331,153 km at 27.48 pc = 0.16 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 36.3896 +/- 0.0163 mas (same row, RUWE 0.93): 27.48 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.476 +/- 0.015 solar radii from Burt et al. 2021, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1231 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162...87B/abstract): 331,153 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.485 +/- 0.024 solar masses from Burt et al. 2021, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1231 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162...87B/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3553 +/- 51 K from Burt et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1231 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162...87B/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Burt et al. 2021, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1231 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....162...87B/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1231.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.769, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
